text: protocols. Chamber Size EBW chamber size is one of the biggest considerations in terms of capital costs. Since these systems can occupy significant floor space, chamber size can also greatly influence the operational expense of the system as well. Consider the 2 following EBW systems: the desktop 7L external EBW versus the recently installed 300,000L Probeam internal gun EBW system installed in at Dynetics, Alabama. Figure 31 (Left) Focus gmbh Powerbeam L8 with 9” diameter x 6” long chamber [61] (Right) 300,000L Probeam internal gun EBW with 22’ x 22’ x 22’ chamber[62] The chamber size is chosen based on the size of assemblies that are planned to be welded, while oversizing the chamber is always prudent to ensure future work. Chamber sizes for high gradient structures are categorized at the high end of non-custom weld chamber sizes. As was discussed previously, internal gun systems require a smaller chamber size than external gun systems. In general, the workspace of the external gun chamber needs Page 30 of 55 “Manufacturing full-scale high gradient copper accelerators: Electron beam welding and allied processes” Prepared for the U.S. Department of Energy ARDAP program to be twice the geometric dimensions of the component being welded in order to get full access to the entire component. In contrast, the workspace of the internal fun chamber need only be large enough to contain the component, and the chamber need only be larger than this space by the volume necessary to contain the motion systems for controlling the internal gun and component. It is prudent to oversize the chamber beyond immediate needs as this large chamber can accommodate larger assemblies and/or future work. This potential for future work needs to be balanced against additional costs of a large chamber, both in terms of the chamber itself as well as the associated floor space. It is common for job shops and production facilities to contain multiple EBW welding systems with different chamber sizes, enabling tailoring of equipment used to the workpieces themselves. CERN currently hosts three PTR welding systems with each chamber shown in the image below Figure 32 Various EBW machine at CERN [63] (Left) SST KS110- G300KM system with a 1.5m x 1.5m x 5m vacuum volume with vertically mounted high voltage gun (Center) Cylindrical PTR EBW machine at CERN, dimensions unknown (Right) Small PTR EBW machine at CERN, dimensions unknown CERN is currently in the process of procuring a forth EBW machine as part of their 7,000 sq ft facility dedicated to in-house fabrication of beryllium beam pipes as part of the high luminosity upgrade [64]. For comparison, Thomas Jefferson National Accelerator Facility (JLab) owns and operates a Sciaky 60kV/700mA internal electron beam welding gun with six-axis CNC controlled gun in a 68” x 68” x 84” stainless steel vacuum with a 6,000 L/s CTI high vacuum cryo pump.
